title: The Role of Similar Accounting Standards in Cross‐Border Mergers and Acquisitions

context.country_region: 32 countries (cross-border M&A country pairs; 32 acquirer countries and 32 target countries)

data_sources.name: Bae, Tan, and Welker's (2008) [21 accounting items / GAAP differences; based on Nobes 2001 survey]
Global Vantage database [firm-level accruals for Comparability metric; voluntary IAS/IFRS adoption control]
Bhattacharya, Daouk, and Welker (2003) [earnings opacity metrics; accounting quality AQ]

analyses.label: Table 3 (cols 1 & 3): OLS of cross-border M&A frequency on GAAP Similarity/Comparability (H1)
analyses.sample: 643 country pairs (32 acquirer x 32 target countries), cross-border M&As 1998-2004

controls.name: Acquirer and target country fixed effects

analyses.label: Table 3 (cols 2 & 4): OLS of cross-border M&A dollar value on GAAP Similarity/Comparability (H1)

dv.name: Volume of cross-border M&A activity (dollar value)

key_ivs.name: Similarity (GAAP similarity)
key_ivs.measure: ratio of the sum of 'GAAP similar' scores across all 21 Bae et al. (2008) accounting items, scaled by 21; range 0 to 1

controls.name: Acquirer and target country fixed effects

analyses.label: Table 4 Panel A: subsample split by public enforcement (strong vs weak) with F-test on Similarity/Comparability coefficient difference (H2)
analyses.sample: strong public-enforcement subsample N=330 vs weak subsample N=313 (country pairs partitioned at median public enforcement)

dv.name: Volume of cross-border M&A activity (frequency and dollar value)

key_ivs.name: Similarity x public enforcement regime (partition)
key_ivs.measure: GAAP Similarity index estimated separately for target countries above vs below the median public enforcement index; F-statistic tests the difference in the Similarity coefficient between strong and weak enforcement subsamples
key_ivs.source: Bae et al. (2008) [Similarity]; La Porta et al. (2006) [public enforcement index]

key_ivs.name: Comparability x public enforcement regime (partition)
key_ivs.measure: accruals Comparability metric estimated separately for strong vs weak public-enforcement target-country subsamples; F-statistic tests coefficient difference
key_ivs.source: Global Vantage database [Comparability]; La Porta et al. (2006) [public enforcement]

controls.name: Full Table 3 country-level control set (economic/capital-market development, cultural familiarity, tax, investor protection, accounting quality, openness)
controls.source: World Bank WDI (2009); CEPII (2008); La Porta et al. (1998/2006); Bhattacharya et al. (2003)

controls.name: Difference in public enforcement across the country pair
Acquirer and target country fixed effects

analyses.label: Table 4 Panel B: subsample split by securities regulation (strong vs weak) with F-test on Similarity/Comparability coefficient difference (H2)
analyses.sample: country pairs partitioned at median securities regulation index into strong vs weak subsamples

dv.name: Volume of cross-border M&A activity (frequency and dollar value)

key_ivs.name: Similarity x securities regulation regime (partition)
key_ivs.measure: GAAP Similarity index estimated separately for target countries above vs below the median securities regulation index; F-statistic tests the coefficient difference
key_ivs.source: Bae et al. (2008) [Similarity]; Hail and Leuz (2006) [securities regulation index]

key_ivs.name: Comparability x securities regulation regime (partition)
key_ivs.measure: accruals Comparability estimated separately for strong vs weak securities-regulation subsamples; F-statistic tests coefficient difference
key_ivs.source: Global Vantage database [Comparability]; Hail and Leuz (2006) [securities regulation]

controls.name: Full Table 3 country-level control set
controls.source: World Bank WDI (2009); CEPII (2008); La Porta et al. (1998/2006); Bhattacharya et al. (2003)

controls.name: Difference in securities regulation across the country pair
Acquirer and target country fixed effects

analyses.label: IFRS mandatory-adoption time-series test: change in cross-border M&A activity around the 2005 mandatory IFRS adoption (identification / robustness for H1 causality)
analyses.sample: IFRS-adopting country pairs, time-series around 2005 (pre- vs post-adoption); public vs private target firms

dv.name: [withheld: wording matches the source]
dv.measure: cross-border M&A activity for country pairs, compared before and after the 2005 mandatory IFRS adoption; examined separately for public (listed) vs private (unlisted) targets

key_ivs.name: Mandatory IFRS adoption (post-2005 period among adopting countries)
key_ivs.measure: time-series indicator for the post-2005 period following widespread mandatory adoption of IFRS; effect examined most sharply for country pairs with low pre-adoption GAAP similarity
key_ivs.source: Bae et al. (2008) [pre-adoption GAAP similarity]; SDC [M&A activity]

controls.name: Country-level controls / country fixed effects (as in main models)
controls.source: World Bank WDI (2009); CEPII (2008); La Porta et al. (1998/2006)

constructs: total costs and beneﬁts of harmonization
